I am 67 years old and have farmed this land in Quzhou for 45 years. My 6 mu are not big, but I know every corner of them. I have a well for irrigation, which is essential because the rain here is never enough. My household has 7 people, but my children and grandchildren work outside, so it is mostly me and my old man managing the fields. We are not young anymore, so we must work smart and not waste labor.

I run a garlic-maize and wheat-maize rotation on my 6 mu. In the cool season, I put 3 mu into garlic and 3 mu into winter wheat. After harvest in late May and early June, I plant summer maize on all 6 mu. This is the system I have used for decades, and it gives me both cash income and grain for the family.

For **garlic**, I planted my own saved *hongshuan* cloves last September. I never buy garlic seed — I keep the best bulbs from the harvest before. I rotary-tilled the field before planting and put down 100 jin of 15-15-15 compound fertilizer as basal. Now that spring has started, I will topdress with another 100 jin of compound fertilizer to push the bulbs to grow big. I will irrigate three times from my well using border flooding. Garlic does not get many bugs here, but weeds are a problem, so I will spray herbicide once. I expect about 3,000 jin per mu this year if the weather cooperates.

For **wheat**, I bought improved seed from the supply shop last autumn — about 30 jin per mu. I also rotary-tilled that plot and applied 100 jin of 18-22-5 compound fertilizer before sowing. This spring, I will topdress once more with 100 jin of the same fertilizer when the wheat starts jointing. I irrigate three times. Aphids sometimes come, so I keep an eye out and spray insecticide twice if I see them. I expect around 1,000 jin per mu.

For **summer maize**, I will plant *denghai605* hybrid seed right after harvesting the garlic and wheat in June. I buy fresh hybrid seed every year because saved seed does not keep its vigor. Because my back is not what it used to be, I plant maize with no-tillage directly into the stubble — this saves a lot of labor and time. I apply 100 jin of 15-15-15 compound fertilizer at planting and that is usually enough; I do not topdress maize. I irrigate three times during the summer. Maize needs more protection, so I spray insecticide, herbicide, and fungicide once each. I expect about 1,000 jin per mu.

This is what I have always done. It feeds my family and pays for the grandchildren's school.
